Elena — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I received invoice_aug_2026.pdf and the sample session IDs. I'm pulling team resources to investigate; copying Ben (billing) to run the metering trace and Kim (finance) for credit-routing if needed.

Quick answers up front:
- "Hourly flattening" is an internal label for an out-of-band aggregation adjustment we apply when short-lived sessions cause noisy per-request extrapolation. It should only show up when we detect churn above a threshold and apply a smoothing/flattening factor.
- That said, it should be attributable to request_ids / session_ids; if it's not mapping cleanly that's a red flag.

Ben — can you run the aggregation trace for NovumTech for the 2026-08-12 01:30–06:00 UTC window and confirm whether HOUR-FLAT-ADJ was applied server-side vs introduced by post-processing? I have included the sample session_ids they provided.

Elena — we'll aim to get an initial update in 24 hours and a proposed remediation/credit within 48–72 hours. Apologies for the friction around your reconciliation cutoff; we'll prioritize.

Best,

Markus / Kim — quick summary from the metering pipeline trace (see billing_analysis_20260818.xlsx attached):

What we traced:
- For NovumTech, between 2026-08-12T01:48:00Z and 2026-08-12T05:22:00Z we observed ~1.2M rapid open/close ephemeral sessions from a small subset of API keys. These match the sample session_ids Elena sent.
- The realtime metering front-end emitted per-request tokens, but our hourly aggregator has a safeguard that, when churn > 60% inside a 15-minute bucket, it applies a "flattening factor" to avoid over-extrapolation from high turnover. That calculation produced an adjustment labelled HOUR-FLAT-ADJ for that hourly window.
- Root cause appears to be client-side session parallelism (short-lived connections) combined with a burst of retries; not a logger duplication on Redwood side. However — there is an edge case: when a session opens and closes within the same minute across multiple workers, our hourly consolidation historically double-counted the KV-cache prefix for ~0.7% of those churned requests. We patched that in 2026-08-16 but the August invoice run included the earlier raw hourly consolidation.

Impact and proposed remediation:
- Total HOUR-FLAT-ADJ line: $1,085.90 (matches invoice)
- We estimate 0.7% of the HOUR-FLAT-ADJ ($7.60) is attributable to our double-counting bug introduced prior to the 8/16 patch. The remainder is legitimate flattening from their observed churn pattern.

Recommendation:
1) Offer a goodwill credit for the patched double-count ($7.60) immediately to NovumTech.
2) For the remaining amount, propose a 60% credit (customer-split) as a concession while we align on best practices for connection patterns — total provisional credit would be $652.54 (60% of $1,085.90) + $7.60 bug credit = $660.14.
3) Create a short technical guidance doc for NovumTech (connection/retry patterns) and schedule a 30-minute postmortem with their infra team.

Please confirm if finance can issue a provisional credit for $660.14 and whether we want to waive the credits against their next invoice or issue a standalone credit memo.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Elena — thanks for your patience. Ben ran the end-to-end trace and we confirmed two things: 1) most of the HOUR-FLAT-ADJ reflects legitimate smoothing against high short-lived session churn, and 2) a very small portion (approx $7.60) was caused by a consolidation edge-case on our side that has already been patched (deploy 2026-08-16).

Proposal: we will issue a provisional credit of $660.14 to NovumTech (details below):
- $7.60 credit for the consolidation duplication we introduced (one-time technical bug).
- $652.54 goodwill credit (60% of remaining HOUR-FLAT-ADJ) to acknowledge the customer impact and to buy time for NovumTech to adopt connection guidance.

How credit is applied:
- Option A (preferred): Issue a credit memo for $660.14 applied against the next invoice. This keeps AP simple and preserves invoice history.
- Option B: Issue a standalone refund if you prefer cash-out; requires FE approval and will take 5–7 business days to process.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm NovumTech preference for Option A vs B by EOD Aug 20 so we can lock in finance routing.
2) Ben will share a short connection/retry guidance doc and schedule a 30-minute sync with NovumTech infra for week of Aug 23.
3) We will mark this incident as CLOSED once the credit is posted and the guidance session is complete.

Elena — if this looks acceptable we will issue the credit memo and send formal confirmation to your AP team.

Best regards,
